visual_language: historically grounded Tang-dynasty Chinese setting rather than generic fantasy Asia
materials, silhouettes and public spaces should read as a coherent 8th-century Chang'an production world
wardrobe_rules: use Tang-period Chinese garment silhouettes, layering and accessories appropriate to character role and status
hair styling and headwear must be chosen per character role, gender presentation and social context
architecture_rules: use Tang-era Chinese timber architecture, courtyard planning, gates, tiled roofs and urban street logic appropriate to Chang'an
keep building scale and ornament consistent within the same social location
prop_rules: use period-plausible lamps, ceramics, paper, writing implements, furnishings, transport and weapons only when story-relevant
environment_rules: weather, vegetation and street dressing should match the selected season and north-central China setting
cinematography: cinematic composition with controlled production design; do not use theme-park or cosplay presentation unless explicitly requested
profiles.casting_policy: Character identity comes from casting. This profile constrains Tang-era Chinese wardrobe, environment and material culture; it does not copy any real person.

visual_language: historically grounded Ming-dynasty Jiangnan setting with coherent domestic, street and water-town material culture
keep costume and architecture tied to the same century and social milieu
wardrobe_rules: use Ming-period Chinese garment silhouettes, collars, layering, belts and headwear appropriate to role and status
do not borrow later Qing-era hair or dress conventions
architecture_rules: use Jiangnan timber-and-masonry dwellings, courtyards, lanes, bridges and waterside structures appropriate to the Ming period
prop_rules: use period-plausible furniture, ceramics, lanterns, books, writing tools, market goods and transport
environment_rules: use humid Jiangnan atmosphere, waterways, planting and street texture only when consistent with the selected location and season
cinematography: naturalistic historical drama framing with restrained production design and believable lived-in surfaces
profiles.casting_policy: Character identity comes from casting. This profile constrains Ming-era Jiangnan wardrobe, environment and material culture; it does not copy any real person.

visual_language: late-Victorian London production world with coherent street, domestic and institutional design
social class and occupation should control wardrobe, interiors and props more than generic period decoration
wardrobe_rules: use late-1890s British silhouettes, tailoring, outerwear, hats, footwear and fabrics appropriate to character class and occupation
architecture_rules: use London brick terraces, stone civic buildings, industrial infrastructure and interiors appropriate to the chosen neighborhood
prop_rules: use period-plausible lighting, print media, transport, furniture, tools and household objects
environment_rules: street dressing, weather and industrial haze should follow the specific scene rather than a permanent fog stereotype
cinematography: cinematic period-drama lighting with realistic materials and restrained production design
profiles.casting_policy: Character identity and ethnicity come from casting. This profile constrains late-Victorian London period design and does not imply a generic European facial type.

visual_language: Belle Époque Paris production world with coherent boulevard, apartment, café and working-city material culture
distinguish elegant, bourgeois and working environments by production design rather than mixing them
wardrobe_rules: use turn-of-the-century French silhouettes, tailoring, dresses, hats, footwear and accessories appropriate to role and class
architecture_rules: use Haussmann-era streets and façades, period shopfronts, cafés and interiors when location-appropriate
prop_rules: use period-plausible bicycles, carriages, early motor vehicles only where justified, printed matter, furniture and lighting
environment_rules: street activity, signage density and weather should be scene-specific and not a postcard caricature
cinematography: cinematic historical realism with warm practicals where motivated and controlled depth of field
profiles.casting_policy: Character identity and ethnicity come from casting. This profile constrains Belle Époque Paris production design and does not imply a generic European facial type.

visual_language: contemporary Berlin location realism with neighborhood-specific architecture and lived-in interiors
avoid reducing the city to a single tourist or nightclub aesthetic
wardrobe_rules: wardrobe follows character age, occupation, subculture, season and socioeconomic context rather than a generic European look
architecture_rules: select architecture by neighborhood and story need: prewar blocks, postwar housing, adaptive reuse, contemporary offices or transit
prop_rules: use contemporary European consumer objects, transit, signage and technology only when scene-relevant
environment_rules: weather, street density, bicycles, transit and public-space behavior should follow the chosen neighborhood and season
cinematography: grounded contemporary European drama photography with location-led color and practical lighting
profiles.casting_policy: Character identity and ethnicity come from casting. This profile defines contemporary Berlin production context and never substitutes a generic European facial type.
